header.running_head: Proceeding in Jihaad in the Path of Allaah with a Sincere Intention

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ! (Tell me about) A person who proceeds in Jihaad with the intention of earning some worldly profits?" Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated, "He shall not be rewarded." Again regarding this to be a very serious matter, the Sahabah (RA) instructed the person to again repeat the question. The man asked for the third time, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! (Tell me about) A person who proceeds in Jihaad with the intention of earning some worldly profits?" Rasulullaah ﷺ again repeated, "He shall not be rewarded."[^1]

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that a man approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with the query, "Tell me about a person who wages Jihaad in search of fame and fortune. What is there for him?" "There shall be nothing for him," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. When the man repeated his question three times, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied each time, "There shall be nothing for him." Thereafter, Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "Allaah accepts only those actions that are carried out solely for Him, through which His pleasure is sought."[^2]

Hadhrat Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah (RA) narrates that a man lived amongst them whose identity no one really knew. He was only known as Quzmaan. Whenever his name was mentioned, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to say, "He is from the inmates of Jahannam." He fought very fiercely during the Battle of Uhud and single-handedly killed seven to eight Mushrikeen. He was a true warrior. However, he was eventually incapacitated by a nasty wound. When he was carried to the Banu Zafar district, many Muslims said to him, "You fought with great courage today, O Quzmaan! Glad tidings to you!" He said, "Glad tidings for what? By Allaah! I fought only for the good name of my people. Had it not been for this, I would never have fought." When his wound became too much for him to bear, he took an arrow from his quiver and used it to commit suicide.[^3]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah (RA)

blocks.text: It is reported that Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) used to often ask (the people around him), "Tell me about the person who entered Jannah without ever performing a single salaah?" When the people were unable to identify the person, they asked Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) about him. Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) would then say, "He was Usayram from the Banu Abdul Ash'hal tribe (whose real name was) Amr bin Thaabit bin Qais."

(One of the narrators) Hadhrat Husayn says that when he asked Hadhrat Mahmood bin Labeed about the story of Hadhrat Usayram (RA), he narrated, "He always refused to accept Islaam when his people invited him. On the day that the Battle of Uhud was fought, it suddenly occurred to him to accept Islaam and he did so. He then took his sword and proceeded until he entered the flanks of the enemy.
